sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.

T his writ appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uccha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaypeeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005 has been filed being aggrieved by the order dated 13.10.2023 passed in Writ Petition No.25128/2023 whereby the writ petition filed by the appellant/petitioner has been dismissed.

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that appellant is a Mawa vendor and 55 buckets of Mawa weighing 1375 kg were seized from the Cold Storage and three samples were sent for testing.

The appellant has filed an application before the competent authority seeking release of seized M a w a on supurdginama which was disposed off vide order dated 14.07.2023 with the pre-condition to deposit Rs. 3,43,000/- in the form of demand draft/bank guarantee with the further condition that the third sample of Mawa sent for test at Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore if found to be contrary to the standard laid down under the Food Safety Act , the demand draft/bank guarantee so deposited shall be encashed.
Against the said order, appellant has preferred writ petition which was dismissed by the order impugned by the learned Single Judge.
Now the present intra Court appeal is filed.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that learned Single has passed the order on wrong consideration of facts, law and contrary to the record of the case.

Learned Single Judge has erred in not considering that as per Section 46(3) of the Food Safety Act and Rule 4.2.5 and 4.2.6 of the Food Safety Rules which provides that on receipt of the sample, the food analyst shall forward the report within 14 days and in case in such time sample is not tested then food analyst shall inform to the designated officers and Food Commissioner giving and specifying the time taken in the analysis which has not been done in the present case.
It is further submitted that food samples were collected from only 03 buckets.
However, entire 55 buckets of Ma wa were seized.

Moreso, while testing third sample which has been tested as per the regulation 2.1.6 of Food Safety and Standard (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011[referred to as 'the Regulation 2011], the referral Food Laboratory Mysore did not mention about the formalin test which is used for preserving food article then in absence of particular test, it cannot be accepted that the sample of Mawa which has been tested by the Referral Food Laboratory was fit for test analysis.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011[referred
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, the said report cannot be relied upon.

Further as per Section 47(1)(C) of the Regulation, 2011, after collecting samples, one part of the sample shall be sent to the Food Analyst and two other parts to the Designated Officer for keeping them in safe custody so that if the one part of the sample sent to the analyst was found to be substandard, adulterated and unsafe, then by invoking the Clause (iii) of Sec 47(1)(C), the vendor of the items seized may request the Designated Officer for retesting of the sample and thereafter, on receiving the report in favour of the vendor, the Designated Officer shall send remaining third part of the sample kept in his custody to the Referral Food Laboratory which has not been followed in the case in hand.
Hence, the report relied upon by the learned Single Judge is vague and cannot be considered against the appellant.
Before sending the second and third samples to the Referral Food Laboratory, no speaking order has been passed.
Even otherwise, one sample of Mawa was found as per norms, but learned Single Judge has not taken the same into consideration.
Hence, the order dated 13.10.2023 deserves to be set aside.
4. We have heard, learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.

sentences.text: It would not be out of place to mention here that out of three samples of Mawa , two samples which were sent to State Laboratory have been found to be of within the standard.
The Food and Safety Officer then sent the same to the Referral Laboratory, Mysore which was not found to be fit for analysis.
Hence, the report of Laboratory cannot be disbelieved.

It is an admitted fact that Ma wa is a perishable item and this Court is afraid that releasing the same after lapse of six months would entail serious consequences a s Mawa may have got rotten by now and if the same is used in preparing sweets etc, by and large it will put health of public at large in danger.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the same cannot be released at this belated stage and, therefore, learned Single Judge has not committed any error in denying the relief as sought for by the appellant by dismissing the writ petition.

6. So far as the oral prayer made by the appellant regarding compensation for the loss incurred to him is concerned, the same cannot be adverted to, in an intra Court appeal.
7.
In view of the aforesaid, the writ appeal fails and is hereby dismissed reserving liberty to the appellant to take recourse to law, if so advised.

(S. A. DHARMADHIKARI)
